104a6a00af.substituent_description: A quinoline-type bicyclic (benzo ring with alternating double bonds fused to a pyridine ring containing N) carries, on the carbon next to ring N, an NH linked to a circle-depicted benzene ring that has a CH3 on the ring carbon directly adjacent (ortho) to the NH-bearing carbon. On the next ring carbon (adjacent to the NH-bearing one) there is a C(=O)-NH-CH2 group, the CH2 being attached to an unsubstituted circle-depicted benzene ring.
104a6a00af.notes: Pencil-style handwritten drawing. In the bicycle the benzo ring has 2 inner double lines and the N-containing ring has 3, giving 5 ring double bonds, plus one C=O. The two plain benzene rings are drawn with circles. NH labels are written with H below N.

c9a3df35bd.substituent_description: A five-membered ring containing N, N, NH, and carbons: one ring N is bonded to a circle-depicted benzene ring bearing Cl para (position 4) to the point of attachment; the ring carbon at the top bears =O, and the ring carbon at the bottom right (double bonded to the lower N) bears an NH linker to a second circle-depicted benzene ring, which carries CO2H para (position 4) to the NH.
c9a3df35bd.notes: Handwritten black ink. Double bonds: one C=O (top of five-membered ring) and one C=N in the five-membered ring. NH linker written with H below N.

a3700ffaac.substituent_description: A carbazole (benzo-pyrrole-benzo tricycle) has an Et on its ring N and, at the carbon of the right-hand benzo ring para to the N-bearing ring carbon (carbazole 3-position), a CH2 linking to the N of a piperidine. The carbon opposite the piperidine N is a spiro carbon shared with a five-membered ring fused to a benzene ring (indane-type); the ring carbon next to the spiro carbon bears OH on a solid wedge, and the next carbon (adjacent to the benzo ring) bears NHAc on a hashed bond.
a3700ffaac.notes: Typeset reference-style structure. Three aromatic rings each drawn with 3 alternating double bonds (9 total). One solid wedge (to OH) and one hashed wedge (to NHAc).

5fa2ce62c7.substituent_description: A five-membered N-ring (pyrrolidine) bearing Boc on its N is spiro-fused at one carbon with a second five-membered ring that contains a C=O and an N and is fused to a circle-depicted benzene ring (oxindole-like). The N of that lactam ring carries a CH2 linked to a circle-depicted benzene ring bearing OCH3 para (position 4) to the CH2.
5fa2ce62c7.notes: Handwritten black ink. The only drawn double bond is the C=O (two parallel strokes, with the O written as a separate circle at the top). OCH3 is written with O stacked above CH3 at the lower right.

98f2b877ee.substituent_description: A bicyclic with a five-membered ring (N, CH, CH2, and two shared carbons) fused to a six-membered ring containing one N: the five-membered ring N bears Ac, the carbon next to that N bears EtOOC, and the next carbon is CH2. In the six-membered ring the N is separated from the fusion carbon (bonded to the Ac-N) by one CH, and the carbon adjacent to that ring N (on the other side) bears OMe.
98f2b877ee.notes: Typeset reference-style structure. Three double bonds all in the six-membered ring (one C=N, two C=C). No carbonyl double bonds are drawn since Ac and EtOOC are written as labels.

a6e343fa47.substituent_description: A circle-depicted benzene ring has, at one position, a carbonyl carbon (drawn as =O above and OEt below) and, para (position 4) to it, a vinyl linkage CH=C(line methyl)-; the alkene carbon bearing a short methyl line is bonded to a second circle-depicted benzene ring at the ring carbon directly adjacent to a ring-fusion carbon. That benzene ring is fused to a saturated six-membered ring whose two carbons next to the fusion each carry two short unlabelled lines (four methyl lines in total: two on the carbon at the top, two on the carbon at the bottom right).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The carbonyl carbon is drawn as a curled C-like stroke, probably a written C label
The t of OEt is written like a plus sign
The aromatic circles are irregular teardrop or D shapes
Methyl lines have small hooked tips and carry no label
The vinyl-bearing carbon of the second ring is attached adjacent to a ring-fusion carbon (exact position on that ring is slightly hard to judge from hand-drawn hexagon)
a6e343fa47.notes: Handwritten black ink on white. Double bonds: one C=O (two vertical strokes) and one alkene C=C (inner short line). The tetralin-like ring system has two aromatic-style circles plus a saturated ring with four plain line substituents.

44593476fa.substituent_description: A fused five-six bicycle (pyrrole ring with N-Me and I on the carbon next to that N, fused to a ring with a ring N=CH, a ring N and a C=O) has its ring N attached through CH2 to the carbon of a piperidine that also bears HO. That piperidine N is acylated by a C(=O) bonded (solid wedge) to the 4-position of a second piperidine, which bears Ph (hashed bond) on the adjacent 3-position and Boc on its ring N.
44593476fa.notes: Typeset reference-style structure. Five double bonds: C=O on the bicycle, ring C=N, two ring C=C in the bicycle, and the amide C=O. Solid wedge goes from the carbonyl-bearing ring carbon toward the C(=O); hashed bond goes to Ph.

906ac61923.substituent_description: An Et label at the left end of a zigzag chain of 10 line vertices ending at an NH, which is bonded to a C(=O) attached to a circle-depicted benzene ring; para (position 4) to that carbonyl is a CH2CH2 chain leading to the 4-position of a piperidine. The piperidine N is bonded to C(=O)-CH2 attached to a second circle-depicted benzene ring bearing, para (position 4) to the CH2, an N carrying two Me labels.
906ac61923.notes: Handwritten black ink on grey paper photographed at a slight angle. Two C=O double bonds drawn as paired strokes. NH is written with H stacked above N. The chain vertex count (10) is between the Et label and the NH.
